# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.

1	/**
2	 * Fleet runs: the deterministic spine of the harness capability program. A
3	 * plan of environment × model × repetition cells runs through the environment
4	 * runner, every cell's report or failure is kept in plan order, and a
5	 * leaderboard is folded from the reports without averaging across isolation
6	 * levels or the held-out split. The
7	 * [four-goal-workflows Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md)
8	 * owns the design rationale.
9	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet
10	 */
11	
12	import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto'
13	import { mkdtemp } from 'node:fs/promises'
14	import { join } from 'node:path'
15	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
16	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
17	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
18	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
19	import type { EnvironmentRunReport } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
20	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
21	import type { EnvironmentDefinition, EnvironmentId, EnvironmentRunModel } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
22	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
23	import type { FleetCell, FleetCellError, FleetCellOutcome, FleetPlan, FleetRunReport, LeaderboardRow } from './types.ts'
24	
25	export type * from './types.ts'
26	
27	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
28	  interface Context {
29	    fleet: FleetService
30	  }
31	}
32	
33	/** Stable error codes of a refused plan. */
34	export type FleetErrorCode = 'FLEET_EMPTY_PLAN' | 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN'
35	
36	/** Error returned by the fleet boundary for a plan that cannot run. */
37	export class FleetError extends HarnessError {
38	  /**
39	   * @param message - human-readable reason.
40	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
41	   */
42	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
43	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
44	  constructor(message: string, code: FleetErrorCode) {
45	    super(message, code)
46	  }
47	}
48	
49	/** Deployment choices of the fleet, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
50	export interface Config {
51	  /** Cells run at the same time; each cell is its own session and workspace. */
52	  maxConcurrent?: number
53	}
54	
55	/** The fleet's choices with every default applied. */
56	export interface ResolvedConfig {
57	  readonly maxConcurrent: number
58	}
59	
60	/**
61	 * Apply the fleet's defaults to a validated config.
62	 * @param config - validated deployment config.
63	 * @returns the resolved choices: one cell at a time unless configured.
64	 */
65	export function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
66	  return { maxConcurrent: config.maxConcurrent ?? 1 }
67	}
68	
69	/** Render a thrown value as a cell error without trusting it. */
70	function cellError(error: unknown): FleetCellError {
71	  if (error instanceof HarnessError) return { code: error.code, message: error.message }
72	  return { message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) }
73	}
74	
75	/** Run `tasks` with at most `limit` in flight, keeping results in task order. */
76	async function bounded<T>(tasks: readonly (() => Promise<T>)[], limit: number): Promise<T[]> {
77	  const results = new Array<T>(tasks.length)
78	  let next = 0
79	  const worker = async (): Promise<void> => {
80	    while (next < tasks.length) {
81	      const index = next
82	      next += 1
83	      results[index] = await (tasks[index] as () => Promise<T>)()
84	    }
85	  }
86	  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, tasks.length) }, worker))
87	  return results
88	}
89	
90	/** Key of the leaderboard row a cell belongs to. */
91	function rowKey(cell: FleetCell): string {
92	  return `${cell.model.provider}�${cell.model.model}�${cell.environment}`
93	}
94	
95	/** Fold the leaderboard from the cell outcomes, one row per model route and environment. */
96	function foldLeaderboard(
97	  outcomes: readonly FleetCellOutcome[],
98	  definitions: ReadonlyMap<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition>,
99	): LeaderboardRow[] {
100	  const rows = new Map<string, LeaderboardRow>()
101	  for (const outcome of outcomes) {
102	    const key = rowKey(outcome.cell)
103	    const definition = definitions.get(outcome.cell.environment) as EnvironmentDefinition
104	    const row = rows.get(key) ?? {
105	      provider: outcome.cell.model.provider,
106	      model: outcome.cell.model.model,
107	      environmentId: outcome.cell.environment,
108	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
109	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
110	      runs: 0,
111	      errors: 0,
112	      certified: 0,
113	      certificateRate: 0,
114	      attemptsMean: 0,
115	      inputTokens: 0,
116	      outputTokens: 0,
117	    }
118	    rows.set(key, 'report' in outcome ? withReport(row, outcome.report) : { ...row, errors: row.errors + 1 })
119	  }
120	  return [...rows.values()]
121	}
122	
123	/** Add one report to a row, recomputing the derived rates. */
124	function withReport(row: LeaderboardRow, report: EnvironmentRunReport): LeaderboardRow {
125	  const runs = row.runs + 1
126	  const certified = row.certified + (report.certified ? 1 : 0)
127	  const attempts = row.attemptsMean * row.runs + report.attempts.length
128	  return {
129	    ...row,
130	    isolation: report.stamp.isolation,
131	    runs,
132	    certified,
133	    certificateRate: certified / runs,
134	    attemptsMean: attempts / runs,
135	    inputTokens: row.inputTokens + (report.usage?.inputTokens ?? 0),
136	    outputTokens: row.outputTokens + (report.usage?.outputTokens ?? 0),
137	  }
138	}
139	
140	/**
141	 * Render a leaderboard as a Markdown table for people; the report stays the record.
142	 * @param report - a fleet run report.
143	 * @returns one table with a header row and one row per leaderboard entry.
144	 */
145	export function leaderboardMarkdown(report: FleetRunReport): string {
146	  const header = '| Model | Environment | Held out | Isolation | Runs | Errors | Certified | Rate | Attempts | Tokens in / out |'
147	  const rule = '|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|'
148	  const lines = report.leaderboard.map(row => (
149	    `| ${row.provider}/${row.model} | ${row.environmentId} | ${row.heldOut ? 'yes' : 'no'} | ${row.isolation ?? '-'} | ${row.runs} | ${row.errors} | ${row.certified} | ${row.certificateRate.toFixed(2)} | ${row.attemptsMean.toFixed(2)} | ${row.inputTokens} / ${row.outputTokens} |`
150	  ))
151	  return [`Fleet run \`${report.group}\``, '', header, rule, ...lines].join('\n') + '\n'
152	}
153	
154	/** Fleet runs (`ctx.fleet`): a plan of environment cells through the runner, with a leaderboard. */
155	export class FleetService extends Service {
156	  static inject = ['environments', 'environmentRuns', 'agentDefaultModel']
157	
158	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
159	    maxConcurrent: z.natural().min(1).default(1),
160	  })
161	
162	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
163	
164	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
165	    super(ctx, 'fleet')
166	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
167	  }
168	
169	  /**
170	   * Run every cell of a plan and fold the leaderboard. A cell whose run
171	   * throws is kept as an error outcome; the fleet run itself rejects only for
172	   * a plan it cannot start.
173	   * @param plan - environments, model routes, repetitions, workspace root, group, and abort signal.
174	   * @returns every cell's outcome in plan order and the leaderboard folded from the reports.
175	   * @throws {@link FleetError} when the plan selects no environment or asks for no repetition.
176	   */
177	  async run(plan: FleetPlan): Promise<FleetRunReport> {
178	    if (!Number.isInteger(plan.repetitions) || plan.repetitions < 1) {
179	      throw new FleetError(`repetitions must be a positive integer, got ${String(plan.repetitions)}`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
180	    }
181	    const definitions = this.select(plan)
182	    if (definitions.size === 0) throw new FleetError('the plan selects no environment', 'FLEET_EMPTY_PLAN')
183	    const models = plan.models.length === 0 ? [this.defaultModel()] : plan.models
184	    const group = plan.group ?? `fleet-${randomUUID()}`
185	    const cells: FleetCell[] = []
186	    for (const environment of definitions.keys()) {
187	      for (const model of models) {
188	        for (let repetition = 0; repetition < plan.repetitions; repetition += 1) cells.push({ environment, model, repetition })
189	      }
190	    }
191	    const outcomes = await bounded(cells.map(cell => () => this.runCell(cell, plan, group)), this.resolved.maxConcurrent)
192	    return { group, cells: outcomes, leaderboard: foldLeaderboard(outcomes, definitions) }
193	  }
194	
195	  /** Resolve the plan's environment selection against the registry, in registry order. */
196	  private select(plan: FleetPlan): Map<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition> {
197	    const selected = 'ids' in plan.environments
198	      ? plan.environments.ids.flatMap((id) => {
199	        const definition = this.ctx.environments.get(id)
200	        if (definition === undefined) throw new FleetError(`environment "${id}" is not registered`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
201	        return [definition]
202	      })
203	      : this.ctx.environments.list(plan.environments.filter)
204	    return new Map(selected.map(definition => [definition.id, definition]))
205	  }
206	
207	  /** The composition's default model route, detached from the selection service. */
208	  private defaultModel(): EnvironmentRunModel {
209	    const selection = this.ctx.agentDefaultModel.currentSelection()
210	    return { provider: selection.provider, model: selection.model }
211	  }
212	
213	  /** Run one cell in a fresh workspace directory; a thrown error becomes the cell's outcome. */
214	  private async runCell(cell: FleetCell, plan: FleetPlan, group: string): Promise<FleetCellOutcome> {
215	    try {
216	      const workspace = await mkdtemp(join(plan.workspaceRoot, 'cell-'))
217	      const report = await this.ctx.environmentRuns.run({
218	        environment: cell.environment,
219	        workspace,
220	        model: cell.model,
221	        repetition: cell.repetition,
222	        group,
223	        ...plan.signal === undefined ? {} : { signal: plan.signal },
224	      })
225	      return { cell, report }
226	    } catch (error: unknown) {
227	      return { cell, error: cellError(error) }
228	    }
229	  }
230	}
231	
232	export default FleetService

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Fleet runs: the deterministic spine of the harness capability program. A plan names environments, model routes, and a repetition count; the fleet runs every environment × model × repetition cell through the environment runner in its own fresh workspace, keeps every cell's report or failure in plan order, and folds a leaderboard with one row per model route and environment. Rows are never averaged across isolation levels or across the held-out split; both stay columns a consumer partitions by. The [four-goal-workflows Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: environments
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
12	- id: agent-default-model
13	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-default-model'
14	  config:
15	    provider: deepseek-official
16	    model: deepseek-v4-flash
17	- id: environment-runner
18	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
19	  config:
20	    isolation: none
21	- id: fleet
22	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
23	  config:
24	    maxConcurrent: 4
25	```
26	
27	| Field | Meaning |
28	|---|---|
29	| `maxConcurrent` (default `1`) | Cells in flight at the same time; each cell is its own session and workspace directory, so the bound is a budget on agents and check processes, not on correctness. |
30	
31	The service requires `environments`, `environmentRuns`, and `agentDefaultModel`. `resolveConfig(config)` is the exported defaulting step.
32	
33	## Service contract
34	
35	`ctx.fleet.run(plan)` takes `environments` (`{ ids }` in the given order, or `{ filter }` resolved against the registry in registration order), `models` (an empty list runs the composition's default route from `agentDefaultModel`), a positive integer `repetitions`, an existing absolute `workspaceRoot`, an optional `group`, and an optional `signal`. It rejects with `FleetError` before running any cell: `FLEET_INVALID_PLAN` for a non-positive or fractional `repetitions` or an id the registry does not hold, `FLEET_EMPTY_PLAN` when the selection matches nothing.
36	
37	Cells are enumerated environment-major, then model, then repetition from `0`, and run through `ctx.environmentRuns.run` with at most `maxConcurrent` in flight. Each cell gets a fresh `cell-*` directory under `workspaceRoot` and carries the plan's `group` (or a minted `fleet-<uuid>`) and its repetition index into the run stamp, so every session of the batch is grouped durably in its own log. A cell whose run throws is kept as `{ cell, error }` with the harness error code when the error had one; the fleet run itself never fails because of one cell.
38	
39	The report carries the `group`, every cell outcome in plan order, and the `leaderboard`: per model route and environment, the environment kind and `heldOut` flag, the `isolation` the runs declared (absent when every cell of the row failed before a run), `runs`, `errors`, `certified`, `certificateRate`, `attemptsMean`, and the summed `inputTokens` and `outputTokens`. `leaderboardMarkdown(report)` renders the same rows as one Markdown table for people; the report stays the record and the session logs stay the authority.
40	
41	## Model Experience
42	
43	None, as the fleet only schedules environment runs; the environment runner owns every model-visible effect of each cell, and nothing the fleet holds enters a model request.
44	
45	#### KV Cache effect
46	
47	None; the fleet neither adds to nor changes any model request.
48	
49	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
50	
51	- **The leaderboard is a fold of one fleet run** — cross-run comparison, paired designs across variants, and confidence intervals read the `environment/run` stamps and certificates from the session logs; this package folds only the reports it just produced.
52	- **Sampling is by repetition count** — group sampling with early stop, per-cell budgets, and retry policies are the caller's until a policy plugin exists.
53	- **Workspaces are never removed** — every `cell-*` directory stays under `workspaceRoot` for inspection; a caller that wants a clean root removes it.
54	- **A cell error carries only code and message** — the thrown error's stack and cause stay in the process, and a cell that failed before its run leaves no session; a cell that ran has every attempt as a `verification/run` event in its own session log, which is where a cross-run fold reads run evidence from.

31	function definition(id: EnvironmentIdType, heldOut: boolean): EnvironmentDefinition {
32	  return {

46	class StubEnvironments extends Service {
47	  readonly definitions = [definition(ROUND_TRIP, false), definition(UNSATISFIABLE, false), definition(RESERVED, true)]
48	  constructor(ctx: Context) {

71	type Script = (request: EnvironmentRunRequest) => EnvironmentRunReport | Promise<EnvironmentRunReport>

73	class StubRuns extends Service {
74	  static current: StubRuns
75	  readonly requests: EnvironmentRunRequest[] = []
76	  script: Script = request => report(request, { certified: true })
77	  inFlight = 0
78	  maxInFlight = 0
79	  constructor(ctx: Context) {
80	    super(ctx, 'environmentRuns')
81	    StubRuns.current = this

83	  async run(request: EnvironmentRunRequest): Promise<EnvironmentRunReport> {
84	    this.requests.push(request)
85	    this.inFlight += 1
86	    this.maxInFlight = Math.max(this.maxInFlight, this.inFlight)
87	    try {
88	      return await this.script(request)
89	    } finally {
90	      this.inFlight -= 1

95	interface ReportShape {
96	  certified: boolean
97	  attempts?: number
98	  usage?: { inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number }
99	}

101	function report(request: EnvironmentRunRequest, shape: ReportShape): EnvironmentRunReport {
102	  const model = request.model ?? DEFAULT_MODEL
103	  const count = shape.attempts ?? 1
104	  const attempts = Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => ({
105	    attempt: index + 1,
106	    results: [{
107	      checkId: CheckId('check'),
108	      status: shape.certified && index === count - 1 ? 'pass' as const : 'fail' as const,
109	      evidence: 'exit 0',
110	    }],
111	    treeHash: HEX,
112	  }))
113	  return {
114	    environment: request.environment,
115	    sessionId: SessionId(`session-${request.environment}-${request.repetition ?? 0}-${model.model}`),
116	    stamp: {
117	      kind: 'environment/run',
118	      version: 1,
119	      environmentId: request.environment,
120	      environmentKind: 'smoke',
121	      heldOut: request.environment === RESERVED,
122	      promptSha256: HEX,
123	      checksSha256: HEX,
124	      contentSha256: HEX,
125	      repetition: request.repetition ?? 0,
126	      ...request.group === undefined ? {} : { group: request.group },
127	      model,
128	      isolation: 'process',
129	    },
130	    attempts,
131	    certified: shape.certified,
132	    ...shape.usage === undefined ? {} : { usage: shape.usage },
133	  }
134	}

140	    heldOut: false,
141	    isolation: 'process',
142	    runs: 2,
143	    errors: 0,
144	    certified: 2,
145	    certificateRate: 1,
146	    attemptsMean: 1,
147	    inputTokens: 0,
148	    outputTokens: 0,
149	    ...overrides,
150	  }
151	}

156	  /** A complete plan over both training environments; `group` is `batch-1` unless the second argument is `null`. */

160	async function harness(config: Config = {}): Promise<Harness> {
161	  const ctx = new Context()
162	  for (const stub of [StubEnvironments, StubDefaultModel, StubRuns]) await ctx.plugin(stub)
163	  await ctx.plugin(FleetService, config)
164	  const root = await mkdtemp(join(tmpdir(), 'fleet-'))
165	  const plan = (overrides: Partial<FleetPlan> = {}, group: string | null = 'batch-1'): FleetPlan => ({
166	    environments: { ids: [ROUND_TRIP, UNSATISFIABLE] },
167	    models: [MODEL_A, MODEL_B],
168	    repetitions: 2,
169	    workspaceRoot: root,
170	    ...group === null ? {} : { group },
171	    ...overrides,
172	  })
173	  return { ctx, root, plan }
174	}

211	      row({ model: 'b', environmentId: UNSATISFIABLE, certified: 0, certificateRate: 0, attemptsMean: 2, inputTokens: 10, outputTokens: 2 }),

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

1	/**
2	 * Scorekeeper: the session log as the dataset. A `sessionFacts` projection
3	 * unit serves one live session's facts, and `ctx.scorekeeper` folds the same
4	 * facts out of persisted logs — one record per session, a scoreboard grouped
5	 * by model route, environment, isolation, and held-out split, and a JSONL
6	 * export. The service reads through the session persistence seam and writes no
7	 * session event. The
8	 * [scorekeeper Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-scorekeeper.md)
9	 * owns the design rationale.
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper
11	 */
12	
13	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
14	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
15	import { z as zod } from 'zod'
16	import type { ZodType } from 'zod'
17	import type { SessionEvent, SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
18	// Type-only: resolves ctx.sessionPersistence.
19	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence'
20	// Type-only: resolves ctx.sessionProjections for the optional unit child.
21	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection'
22	import { applySessionFacts, emptySessionFactsState, foldSessionFacts } from './fold.ts'
23	import type { SessionFactsState } from './fold.ts'
24	import { foldScoreboard } from './scoreboard.ts'
25	import type {
26	  FactsExportReport,
27	  FactsExportRequest,
28	  LeaderboardFilter,
29	  ScoreboardBatch,
30	  ScorekeeperSkip,
31	  SessionFacts,
32	  SessionFactsRecord,
33	} from './types.ts'
34	
35	export type * from './types.ts'
36	export {
37	  applySessionFacts,
38	  emptySessionFactsState,
39	  foldSessionFacts,
40	  foldSessionFactsState,
41	} from './fold.ts'
42	export type { SessionFactsState } from './fold.ts'
43	export { foldScoreboard, unbiasedPassAtK } from './scoreboard.ts'
44	export type { ScoreboardFold } from './scoreboard.ts'
45	
46	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
47	  interface Context {
48	    scorekeeper: ScorekeeperService
49	  }
50	}
51	
52	/** Wire payload schema of one run stamp's fields inside the projection. */
53	const environmentSchema = zod.object({
54	  environmentId: zod.string().min(1),
55	  environmentKind: zod.string().min(1),
56	  heldOut: zod.boolean(),
57	  repetition: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
58	  group: zod.string().min(1).optional(),
59	  contentSha256: zod.string().min(1),
60	  provider: zod.string().min(1),
61	  model: zod.string().min(1),
62	  isolation: zod.union([zod.literal('none'), zod.literal('process'), zod.literal('host')]),
63	})
64	
65	// Cast for the optional values: under exactOptionalPropertyTypes zod infers
66	// `T | undefined` where the interface declares absent-or-present fields.
67	/** Wire payload schema of the `sessionFacts` projection (the four fact groups). */
68	const sessionFactsSchema: ZodType<SessionFacts> = zod.object({
69	  identity: zod.object({
70	    environment: environmentSchema.optional(),
71	    requestProvider: zod.string().min(1).optional(),
72	    requestModel: zod.string().min(1).optional(),
73	  }),
74	  outcome: zod.object({
75	    reward: zod.union([zod.literal(1), zod.literal(0), zod.null()]),
76	    rewardBasis: zod.union([
77	      zod.literal('certificate'),
78	      zod.literal('uncertified-completion'),
79	      zod.literal('none'),
80	    ]),
81	    certified: zod.boolean(),
82	    certificateRevision: zod.number().int().positive().optional(),
83	    runsRecorded: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
84	    attempts: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
85	    directives: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
86	    relaxations: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
87	    goalPhase: zod.union([
88	      zod.literal('active'),
89	      zod.literal('paused'),
90	      zod.literal('blocked'),
91	      zod.literal('complete'),
92	    ]).optional(),
93	    goalRoundsStarted: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
94	    goalRoundsCap: zod.number().int().positive().optional(),
95	    budgetBreachCap: zod.string().min(1).optional(),
96	  }),
97	  efficiency: zod.object({
98	    turns: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
99	    steps: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
100	    inputTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
101	    outputTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
102	    cacheReadTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
103	    cacheWriteTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
104	    reasoningTokens: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
105	    wallMs: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
106	  }),
107	  tools: zod.object({
108	    toolCalls: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
109	    toolCallsByName: zod.record(zod.string(), zod.number().int().nonnegative()),
110	    toolErrors: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
111	    toolTimeouts: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
112	    toolAborts: zod.number().int().nonnegative(),
113	  }),
114	}) as unknown as ZodType<SessionFacts>
115	
116	/**
117	 * Projection-grade transition of the `sessionFacts` unit. The outcome group is
118	 * decided by the strict goal and verification folds, so a change they reject
119	 * leaves the value at its previous state instead of tearing the read side;
120	 * validating a written change is the write side's job.
121	 * @param state - the accumulator covering all prior events.
122	 * @param event - the next committed session event.
123	 * @returns the next accumulator, or the same reference when the change was rejected.
124	 */
125	export function applySessionFactsProjection(state: SessionFactsState, event: SessionEvent): SessionFactsState {
126	  try {
127	    return applySessionFacts(state, event)
128	  } catch (_rejectedOutcomeChange) {
129	    // The goal and verification services own the two streams that can throw
130	    // here; their own invariant companions reject a malformed change at source.
131	    return state
132	  }
133	}
134	
135	/** Deployment choices of the scorekeeper, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
136	export interface Config {
137	  /** Repetition draws the scoreboard estimates pass@k for. */
138	  passAtK?: number[]
139	}
140	
141	/** The scorekeeper's choices with every default applied. */
142	export interface ResolvedConfig {
143	  /** Ascending, de-duplicated pass@k draws. */
144	  readonly passAtK: readonly number[]
145	}
146	
147	/**
148	 * Apply the scorekeeper's defaults to a validated config.
149	 * @param config - validated deployment config.
150	 * @returns the resolved choices: pass@1 alone unless configured otherwise.
151	 */
152	export function resolveConfig(config: Config): ResolvedConfig {
153	  return { passAtK: [...new Set(config.passAtK ?? [1])].sort((left, right) => left - right) }
154	}
155	
156	/** Render a read or fold failure for a report without trusting the thrown value. */
157	function reasonOf(error: unknown): string {
158	  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
159	}
160	
161	/** One session's facts, or the failure that prevented folding them. */
162	type FactsOutcome = { readonly record: SessionFactsRecord } | { readonly skip: ScorekeeperSkip }
163	
164	/** Scorekeeper (`ctx.scorekeeper`): session facts, the scoreboard, and the facts export. */
165	export class ScorekeeperService extends Service {
166	  static inject = ['sessionPersistence']
167	
168	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
169	    passAtK: z.array(z.natural().min(1)).default([1]),
170	  })
171	
172	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
173	
174	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config = {}) {
175	    super(ctx, 'scorekeeper')
176	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
177	    // The `sessionFacts` projection unit activates only when a projection
178	    // registry is composed; a headless assembly keeps the service verbs alone.
179	    ctx.inject(['sessionProjections'], (projectionCtx) => {
180	      projectionCtx.sessionProjections.register<'sessionFacts', SessionFactsState>({
181	        key: 'sessionFacts',
182	        schema: sessionFactsSchema,
183	        init: emptySessionFactsState,
184	        apply: applySessionFactsProjection,
185	        view: state => state.facts,
186	        stateVersion: 1,
187	      })
188	    })
189	  }
190	
191	  /**
192	   * Fold one persisted session into its facts record.
193	   * @param sessionId - the persisted session to read.
194	   * @returns the four fact groups with the stored header's identity.
195	   * @throws when the session cannot be read, or its goal or verification stream is malformed.
196	   */
197	  async facts(sessionId: SessionId): Promise<SessionFactsRecord> {
198	    const { meta, events } = await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect(sessionId)
199	    return foldSessionFacts(meta, events)
200	  }
201	
202	  /**
203	   * Fold a scoreboard from persisted session logs, one row per model route,
204	   * environment, isolation level, and held-out split. A session that cannot be
205	   * read or folded is reported and the fold continues.
206	   * @param filter - the sessions to fold and the group and held-out conditions a stamped session must meet.
207	   * @returns the rows with their pass@k statistics, the counts of excluded, unstamped, and skipped sessions, and the fold time.
208	   */
209	  async leaderboard(filter: LeaderboardFilter = {}): Promise<ScoreboardBatch> {
210	    const sessions = await this.sessionsOf(filter.sessions)
211	    const records: SessionFactsRecord[] = []
212	    const skipped: ScorekeeperSkip[] = []
213	    for (const sessionId of sessions) {
214	      const outcome = await this.factsOf(sessionId)
215	      if ('skip' in outcome) skipped.push(outcome.skip)
216	      else records.push(outcome.record)
217	    }
218	    const fold = foldScoreboard(records, filter, this.resolved.passAtK)
219	    return {
220	      rows: fold.rows,
221	      sessions: sessions.length,
222	      excluded: fold.excluded,
223	      unstamped: fold.unstamped,
224	      skipped,
225	      computedAt: Date.now(),
226	    }
227	  }
228	
229	  /**
230	   * Write one JSON line per session's facts record. A session that cannot be
231	   * read or folded is reported and the export continues; the sink is closed
232	   * exactly once when every session has been handled.
233	   * @param request - sessions to export and the destination sink.
234	   * @returns counts of sessions, written lines, and skips with reasons.
235	   */
236	  async exportFacts(request: FactsExportRequest): Promise<FactsExportReport> {
237	    const sessions = await this.sessionsOf(request.sessions)
238	    const skipped: ScorekeeperSkip[] = []
239	    let exported = 0
240	    try {
241	      for (const sessionId of sessions) {
242	        const outcome = await this.factsOf(sessionId)
243	        if ('skip' in outcome) {
244	          skipped.push(outcome.skip)
245	          continue
246	        }
247	        await request.sink.write(`${JSON.stringify(outcome.record)}\n`)
248	        exported += 1
249	      }
250	    } finally {
251	      await request.sink.close()
252	    }
253	    return { sessions: sessions.length, exported, skipped }
254	  }
255	
256	  /** The requested sessions, or every persisted session when none were named. */
257	  private async sessionsOf(sessions?: readonly SessionId[]): Promise<readonly SessionId[]> {
258	    return sessions ?? (await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.list()).map(header => header.id)
259	  }
260	
261	  /** Read and fold one session, keeping a read or fold failure as a skip. */
262	  private async factsOf(sessionId: SessionId): Promise<FactsOutcome> {
263	    try {
264	      return { record: await this.facts(sessionId) }
265	    } catch (error: unknown) {
266	      return { skip: { sessionId, reason: reasonOf(error) } }
267	    }
268	  }
269	}
270	
271	export default ScorekeeperService

1	# Agent Note: The scorekeeper
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-scorekeeper.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	Every number a fleet run reports today lives only in the process that produced it. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet` folds a `LeaderboardRow` from the reports its own `run()` collected, so the leaderboard dies with the process: a restart, a second batch, or a question asked a week later has nothing to fold. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) states the opposite principle — the log is the dataset, and every metric must be recomputable from first principles — and names a Scoreboard row schema of 180 fields across eight groups, a `SessionFacts` projection, and an `EnvironmentStats` fold that W1 stage 2 and W3 stage 2 both read.
10	
11	Two gaps sit between that principle and the code. Nothing folds a session log into per-session facts, so a consumer that wants turns, tokens, tool behavior, or the attempt count has to re-derive each of them from the raw events. And nothing measures difficulty: the runner already stamps every session with its environment, group, and repetition, but no fold turns a group of repetitions into pass@k, so a suite plan has no measured difficulty to select on and a calibration stage has nothing to read.
12	
13	The 180-field schema is also not buildable today. Most of its groups — process quality, judge scores, safety and oversight, training and data — name fields whose source events do not exist: `signoff/recorded`, the composition manifest, the oversight monitor's verdicts, the judge council's scores, the curator's consent and redaction records. Shipping them as nullable columns would put empty fields in a training dataset and invite a consumer to read a `null` as a measurement.
14	
15	## Proposal
16	
17	Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper` (`ctx.scorekeeper`) to the `improvement/` group: the fold that turns session logs into rows, and nothing else.
18	
19	**Four groups, every field from a named event.** `SessionFacts` ships identity and provenance, outcome, efficiency, and tool behavior. A field exists only when a session event carries it today: the `environment/run` stamp supplies the cell identity, `request/header` the requested route, `goal/change` and the five `verification/*` events the outcome, `budget/breach` the cap that stopped a session, `turn/start`, `step/start` and `assistant/message` usage the efficiency, and `tool/call` and `tool/result` the tool behavior. The four remaining groups of the note's schema ship nothing until their producers exist, and the package README names them under Known Limitations so their absence is a recorded gap rather than a silent one. Field names are camelCase in TypeScript and in every export, unlike the note's snake_case sketch.
20	
21	**One fold, two faces.** `applySessionFacts` is the incremental transition and `foldSessionFacts(meta, events)` the whole-log entry; the `sessionFacts` projection unit registers the first on `ctx.sessionProjections` under `ctx.inject`, and the service runs the second over persisted logs. Both therefore produce the same value, and a live carrier and an offline scoreboard can never drift. The outcome group is decided by the folds that already own those streams — `foldTrajectoryReward` (extracted from the trajectory fold for this purpose), `foldVerification`, and `foldGoal` — so the reward a scoreboard row reports is the reward a trajectory line reports, by construction rather than by review. The accumulator keeps the goal, verification, and budget events and refolds them whenever one arrives; the projection unit wraps the strict folds so a rejected change leaves the served value untouched instead of tearing the read side.
22	
23	**The scoreboard is grouped, never averaged.** A row is one model route on one environment at one isolation level and one side of the held-out split, exactly the partitioning the fleet's leaderboard already respects. `runs` counts sessions that recorded at least one `verification/run` and `errors` the stamped sessions that recorded none, so a cell that ended without a run is a column rather than a missing row — the note's survivorship risk, answered. A session with no `environment/run` stamp names no cell and is counted apart.
24	
25	**`EnvironmentStats` is pass@k over the batches the runner already stamps.** Each session's stamp carries a `group` and a `repetition`; the sessions sharing a group are one batch of `n` samples of which `c` certified, and pass@k for that batch is the unbiased `1 - C(n - c, k) / C(n, k)`, evaluated as a product so no factorial overflows. A row's estimate is the mean over the batches holding at least `k` sessions; a batch smaller than `k` contributes nothing and a `k` no batch reached is absent from the row. The `k` list is `Config`, because how many repetitions a deployment can afford is a deployment choice.
26	
27	**Nothing is written.** The service reads through the session persistence seam and appends no event, so composing it changes no session log. `exportFacts` writes one JSON line per session through the trajectory exporter's `TrajectorySink`, so a deployment that already has a sink for trajectories has one for facts.
28	
29	## Alternatives considered
30	
31	**Persist a scoreboard store.** A durable table of rows written as runs finish would answer a query without re-reading logs. It is rejected because a stored row is a second source of truth that a schema change silently invalidates, and because the note's P3 makes the log the dataset: re-reading is the property, not the cost. A cache belongs behind the same fold once one is measured to be needed.
32	
33	**Ship the note's 180 fields as nullable columns.** Shipping every named field with `null` where no producer exists would let downstream schemas stabilize early. It is rejected because a `null` in a training or evaluation record is indistinguishable from a measured absence, and because the note itself states that a metric without a source event is not a field.
34	
35	**Fold the scoreboard inside `dsh-fleet`.** The fleet already folds a leaderboard, so extending it to read persisted logs would need no new package. It is rejected because the fleet's leaderboard is a fold of one in-memory run and its rows die with the process, while a scoreboard must answer over every session any composition ever persisted; keeping both makes the e2e comparison between them a real cross-check rather than a tautology.
36	
37	**Duplicate the reward rules.** The outcome group could restate the trajectory fold's reward decision instead of extracting `foldTrajectoryReward`. It is rejected because two copies of "what counts as certified" is exactly the drift a leaderboard cannot survive; the extraction is behavior-preserving and the invariant companion checks the two folds still agree on every certificate.
38	
39	**Snake_case field names.** The note sketches `session_id`, `reward_outcome`, and so on. It is rejected because every other record in this repository is camelCase in TypeScript and on the wire, and a consumer reading trajectories and facts side by side should not switch conventions between them; a trainer that wants snake_case renames at its own boundary.
40	
41	## Acceptance criteria
42	
43	- The `sessionFacts` projection unit appears in `ctx.sessionProjections.snapshot(session).values` when the scorekeeper is composed beside a projection registry, disappears when the service fiber is disposed, and leaves its served value untouched when the strict goal or verification fold rejects a change.
44	- Every shipped field is tabulated in the package README against the session event it folds from, and no field folds from anything else.
45	- `ctx.scorekeeper.leaderboard()` over the logs of a fleet run agrees with that fleet run's own in-memory leaderboard on `runs`, `certified`, `certificateRate`, and `attemptsMean` for every cell, proven by a Loader-booted example (`examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/scoreboard`).
46	- `ctx.scorekeeper.facts()` for a certified session carries reward `1` with basis `certificate`, the recorded run count, and non-zero token and tool counts; `exportFacts` writes one line per session and closes its sink exactly once.
47	- A stamped session that recorded no `verification/run` is an `errors` column of its row, and a session with no stamp is counted as `unstamped` rather than dropped.
48	- The package invariant recomputes `runsRecorded` against the raw count of `verification/run` events, `certified` against the reward fold's verdict, and a certificate's isolation against the isolation its `environment/run` stamp declared, and a keyless test proves the last relation rejects a certificate earned under another isolation level.
49	
50	## Rollout
51	
52	1. This note, the package, the `sessionFacts` projection unit, the scoreboard with pass@k, the JSONL export, and the Loader-booted example over the fleet-run stack.
53	2. Per-cell budgets from the fleet plan surfaced as facts, once the budget policy reads them: a breached cap is already a field, the configured limit is not.
54	3. The groups whose producers arrive later — process quality with `signoff/recorded` and the composition manifest, safety and oversight with the monitor's verdicts, training and data with the curator's consent and redaction records — each added with its producer, never ahead of it.
55	4. Cross-run comparison: paired designs, bootstrap confidence intervals, and cost per certified session belong to the experiment plugin the [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) names, reading these rows rather than replacing them.
56	
57	## Risks
58	
59	Refolding the kept goal and verification events on every such event is quadratic in their number. A session records a handful per attempt, so the cost is bounded in practice; a session that recorded thousands of verification changes would pay for it, and an incremental strict fold whose state is plain JSON is the fix if one ever appears.
60	
61	The `sessionFacts` value changes on every committed event because `wallMs` spans the log, so a subscribed carrier is notified once per event rather than once per meaningful change. Dropping `wallMs` from the projection would restore the quiet path at the cost of a field the note names; the churn is accepted and recorded in the README instead.
62	
63	A scoreboard folded over every persisted session mixes whatever a composition happens to have stored. The `group` filter is the only defence against comparing cells from unrelated batches, and a consumer that omits it gets an average across runs it did not intend; cross-run comparison stays the experiment plugin's job for exactly this reason.
64	
65	Pass@k over a batch assumes the batch's sessions are independent samples of one cell. A deployment that reuses one `group` across environments or model routes still gets per-row batches, because a row is already partitioned by both, but a deployment that reuses a `group` across two fleet runs of the same cell will see them pooled.
66

1 # Environments and trajectories 2 3 English | [中文](improvement.zh.md) 4 5 Types shared by the improvement seam. An environment declares one task with executable checks in the completion-standard vocabulary; the runner runs it as one fresh session and stamps the log with what ran; the fleet runs a plan of environment × model × repetition cells and folds a leaderboard; a trajectory is one persisted session folded into the `dsh-trajectory/1` record a trainer reads, with the reward a certificate decided; session facts are the same session folded into the row a scoreboard is grouped from. The [trajectory-export](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md), [environment-runner](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-environment-runner.md), [scorekeeper](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-scorekeeper.md), and [four-goal-workflows](../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) Agent Notes own the design; this page records the exact fields from [`packages/improvement/environments/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/environments/src/types.ts), [`packages/improvement/fleet/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/fleet/src/types.ts), [`packages/improvement/trajectories/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/trajectories/src/types.ts), and [`packages/improvement/scorekeeper/src/types.ts`](../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/src/types.ts). 6 7 ## Environment definition 8 9 `EnvironmentId` is a [branded id](core.md#branded-ids). The `checks` are the same `StandardCheck` values a validator authors a completion standard from, so evaluation and production measure the same outcomes; `heldOut` marks tasks reserved for evaluation. 10 11 ```ts type-equiv 12 /** The work an environment asks of an agent. */ 13 interface EnvironmentTask { 14 /** Complete task statement handed to the agent as its first user message. */ 15 readonly prompt: string 16 /** Workspace fixture the runner mounts before the task starts, absent for a task that needs no files. */ 17 readonly fixture?: string 18 } 19 ``` 20 21 ## Run stamp 22 23 The runner appends one `environment/run` event before a run's first turn. It is the durable link from a session to its environment: every fold that groups, decontaminates, or ranks sessions by environment reads it from the log, and the exporter withholds held-out sessions by it. 24 25 ```ts type-equiv 26 /** 27 * Durable link from a session to the environment it ran, written by the 28 * runner as the `environment/run` event before the run's first turn. Every 29 * fold that groups, decontaminates, or ranks sessions by environment reads it 30 * from the log instead of from an in-memory report. 31 */ 32 interface EnvironmentRunStamp extends EnvironmentContentHashes { 33 readonly kind: 'environment/run' 34 readonly version: 1 35 /** Environment that was run. */ 36 readonly environmentId: EnvironmentId 37 /** Declared kind of the environment. */ 38 readonly environmentKind: string 39 /** Whether the environment is reserved for evaluation; exports drop held-out sessions unless asked to keep them. */ 40 readonly heldOut: boolean 41 /** Zero-based repetition of this environment inside its batch; paired designs match repetitions across variants. */ 42 readonly repetition: number 43 /** Batch or sampling group the run belongs to, absent for a single run. */ 44 readonly group?: string 45 /** Model route the implementer ran on. */ 46 readonly model: EnvironmentRunModel 47 /** Isolation the deployment declared for the run's checks. */ 48 readonly isolation: CertificateIsolation 49 } 50 ``` 51 52 ## Leaderboard row 53 54 The fleet folds one row per model route and environment from the reports of one fleet run. A row never averages across isolation levels or across the held-out split: `isolation` and `heldOut` are columns a consumer partitions by, and a row whose cells all failed before a run carries no isolation claim. 55 56 ```ts type-equiv 57 /** 58 * One leaderboard row: one model route on one environment. Rows are never 59 * averaged across isolation levels or across the held-out split; both are 60 * columns a consumer partitions by. 61 */ 62 interface LeaderboardRow { 63 readonly provider: string 64 readonly model: string 65 readonly environmentId: EnvironmentId 66 readonly environmentKind: string 67 readonly heldOut: boolean 68 /** Isolation the runs declared, absent when every cell of the row failed before a run. */ 69 readonly isolation?: CertificateIsolation 70 /** Cells that produced a report. */ 71 readonly runs: number 72 /** Cells that produced no report. */ 73 readonly errors: number 74 /** Reported cells whose run certified. */ 75 readonly certified: number 76 /** `certified / runs`, `0` without runs. */ 77 readonly certificateRate: number 78 /** Mean attempts over reported cells, `0` without runs. */ 79 readonly attemptsMean: number 80 /** Summed model usage over reported cells. */ 81 readonly inputTokens: number 82 readonly outputTokens: number 83 } 84 ``` 85 86 ## Trajectory reward 87 88 The reward carries its basis: `certificate` when a completion standard existed for the goal (the verifier decided, `1` with a covering certificate and `0` without), `uncertified-completion` when the goal completed with no standard ever authored, and `none` when the log holds no goal. 89 90 ```ts type-equiv 91 /** The reward with its basis and the evidence behind it. */ 92 interface TrajectoryReward { 93 /** `1` for a certified completion, `0` for a measured goal without a covering certificate, `null` when no verifier decided. */ 94 readonly outcome: 1 | 0 | null 95 readonly basis: TrajectoryRewardBasis 96 /** Goal the reward measures, absent when the log holds none. */ 97 readonly goal?: TrajectoryGoal 98 /** Certificate covering the current standard revision, present only when `outcome` is `1`. */ 99 readonly certificate?: VerificationCertificate 100 /** Directives the validator issued during the session. */ 101 readonly directives: number 102 /** Checks relaxed out of the standard during the session. */ 103 readonly relaxations: number 104 /** Runs of the standard recorded during the session, passing or failing. */ 105 readonly attempts: number 106 } 107 ``` 108 109 Messages are projected from the session surface after compaction replacements, each carrying the seq of its source event; token ids and logprobs are absent because the harness never sees them. 110 111 ## Session facts 112 113 The scorekeeper folds one session log into four groups, served both as the `sessionFacts` projection value of a live session and as the record `ctx.scorekeeper.facts()` reads out of persistence. Every field folds from a named session event; the source event of each one is tabulated in [the package README](../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md). 1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	The session log as the dataset. A `sessionFacts` projection unit folds one live session into four fact groups, and `ctx.scorekeeper` folds the same groups out of persisted logs: one record per session, a scoreboard grouped by model route, environment, isolation level, and held-out split, and a JSONL export. The service reads through the session persistence seam and writes no session event. The [scorekeeper Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-scorekeeper.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: persistence
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
12	  config:
13	    root: './.sessions'
14	- id: scorekeeper
15	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper'
16	  config:
17	    passAtK: [1, 8]
18	```
19	
20	| Key | Default | Meaning |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| `passAtK` | `[1]` | Repetition draws the scoreboard estimates pass@k for. Sorted and de-duplicated; a `k` no batch of the row reached is absent from that row. |
23	
24	The service requires a session persistence backend. It registers the `sessionFacts` projection unit only when a projection registry (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection`) is composed.
25	
26	## Service contract
27	
28	`ctx.scorekeeper.facts(sessionId)` reads one persisted session through `ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect()` and returns its `SessionFactsRecord`; a session that cannot be read, or whose goal or verification stream is malformed, rejects.
29	
30	`ctx.scorekeeper.leaderboard({ sessions?, group?, heldOut? })` folds each named session (or every persisted session when `sessions` is absent) and groups the stamped ones into rows. A session that cannot be read or folded is added to `skipped` with its reason and the fold continues; a session whose log carries no `environment/run` stamp is counted as `unstamped` because no row can name its cell; a stamped session the `group` or `heldOut` condition rejects is counted as `excluded`.
31	
32	`ctx.scorekeeper.exportFacts({ sessions?, sink })` writes `JSON.stringify(record) + '\n'` per session to `sink.write()` and closes the sink exactly once, after the last write or after a failure. The sink is the trajectory exporter's `TrajectorySink`, so `jsonlFileSink(path)` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories` serves both exports.
33	
34	`foldSessionFacts(meta, events)` is the pure projection behind all three and is exported for tests and offline tools, together with the incremental `applySessionFacts` the projection unit drives, the `foldScoreboard` row fold, and `unbiasedPassAtK`.
35	
36	## Fact groups and their source events
37	
38	Every field folds from a named session event; nothing is inferred. Field names are camelCase in TypeScript and in every export.
39	
40	### Identity and provenance
41	
42	| Field | Source |
43	|---|---|
44	| `sessionId`, `createdAt` | The stored session header (`facts()` and `exportFacts()` only; a projection value is already addressed by its session) |
45	| `environment.environmentId`, `.environmentKind`, `.heldOut`, `.repetition`, `.group`, `.contentSha256`, `.provider`, `.model`, `.isolation` | The `environment/run` stamp, absent for a session no runner stamped |
46	| `requestProvider`, `requestModel` | `config.provider` and `config.model` of the last `request/header` |
47	
48	### Outcome
49	
50	| Field | Source |
51	|---|---|
52	| `reward`, `rewardBasis` | The trajectory reward fold over `goal/change` and the `verification/*` events |
53	| `certified`, `certificateRevision` | The verification fold's certificate for the current standard revision |
54	| `runsRecorded` | `verification/run` events, passing or failing |
55	| `attempts` | The `attempt` of the last `verification/run`; it restarts at one for each authored standard |
56	| `directives` | `verification/directive` events |
57	| `relaxations` | Relaxed checks of the current standard (`verification/relaxation`) |
58	| `goalPhase`, `goalRoundsCap` | The current `goal/change` snapshot |
59	| `goalRoundsStarted` | Admitted continuation rounds, from the goal fold over `goal/change` and goal-sourced `user/message` |
60	| `budgetBreachCap` | The `cap` of the last `budget/breach` |
61	
62	### Efficiency
63	
64	| Field | Source |
65	|---|---|
66	| `turns`, `steps` | `turn/start` and `step/start` events |
67	| `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `reasoningTokens` | `usage` of every `assistant/message`; the earlier `assistant/chunk` sample for the same step is deliberately not counted twice |
68	| `wallMs` | The first and last event times of the log |
69	
70	### Tool behavior
71	
72	| Field | Source |
73	|---|---|
74	| `toolCalls`, `toolCallsByName` | `tool/call` events |
75	| `toolErrors` | `tool/result` events whose model-facing block reported an error |
76	| `toolTimeouts` | Those whose `error.code` is `TOOL_TIMEOUT` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-call-timeout-policy`) |
77	| `toolAborts` | Those whose `error.code` is `ABORTED` or `ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`) |
78	
79	## Scoreboard rows
80	
81	A row is one model route on one environment at one isolation level and one side of the held-out split; a row never averages across isolation or the split. `runs` counts the sessions that recorded at least one `verification/run` and `errors` the stamped sessions that recorded none, so a cell that ended without a run is a column rather than a missing row. `certificateRate` is `certified / runs` and `attemptsMean` the mean `runsRecorded` over the sessions with runs, both `0` without runs; the token sums cover every session of the row, the errored ones included.
82	
83	`stats` estimates difficulty from the repetition batches the row's sessions belong to: for each batch of `n` sessions of which `c` certified, pass@k is the unbiased `1 - C(n - c, k) / C(n, k)`, and the row's value is the mean over the batches holding at least `k` sessions. A session whose stamp carries no `group` joins no batch.
84	
85	## Model Experience
86	
87	None, as the scorekeeper folds committed events into a projection value and reads persisted logs; it adds nothing to any model request.
88	
89	#### KV Cache effect
90	
91	None; the service neither adds to nor changes any model request.
92	
93	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
94	
95	- **The projection value changes on every event** — `wallMs` spans the log, so no committed event leaves the `sessionFacts` state reference untouched and a subscribed carrier is notified once per event.
96	- **Field groups without a source event** — process quality, judge scores, safety and oversight, and training and data are named by the [four-goal-workflows note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) but ship no field here: `signoff/recorded`, the composition manifest, the oversight monitor, the judge council, and the curator's consent and redaction events do not exist yet.
97	- **Shell exit codes are not observable** — a bash result's exit code travels inside the tool's own model-facing output rather than a session-event field, so `shellNonzeroExits` is not a field; a tool-owned result event would be needed first.
98	- **Cost is not a field** — pricing lives in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy`'s configuration rather than in the log, so a facts record states tokens and names a breached cap but never a EUR amount.
99	- **One standard per session** — the outcome group reads the session's verification fold, which holds one completion standard; a session measuring several goals is scored by the standard in force.
100	- **Rows are not comparable across fleet runs** — a scoreboard folds whatever the filter selects; paired designs, confidence intervals, and cross-run comparison belong to the experiment plugin the four-goal note names.
101

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	/**
3	 * Test driver: boot the scoreboard composition, run the training-eligible
4	 * environments twice each on the default route, then fold the same cells back
5	 * out of the persisted logs — a scoreboard, the facts of the first certified
6	 * cell, and a JSONL export to `./facts.jsonl` — and print both the fleet's
7	 * in-memory leaderboard and the log-derived one for the e2e's assertions.
8	 */
9	
10	import { boot, resolveConfigPath } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot'
11	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
12	import { jsonlFileSink } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'
13	
14	const configPath = process.argv[2]
15	if (configPath === undefined) throw new Error('scoreboard driver requires a config path')
16	
17	const ctx = await boot('scoreboard-e2e', resolveConfigPath(configPath, undefined))
18	try {
19	  // Loader siblings mount concurrently; the runner creates agents only over the settled application.
20	  await ctx.get('loader')?.await()
21	  const fleet = ctx.get('fleet')
22	  const scorekeeper = ctx.get('scorekeeper')
23	  if (fleet === undefined || scorekeeper === undefined) throw new Error('scoreboard driver requires the fleet and the scorekeeper service')
24	  const report = await fleet.run({
25	    environments: { filter: { heldOut: false } },
26	    models: [],
27	    repetitions: 2,
28	    workspaceRoot: process.cwd(),
29	    group: 'scoreboard-e2e',
30	  })
31	  const certified = report.cells.find(outcome => 'report' in outcome && outcome.report.certified)
32	  if (certified === undefined || !('report' in certified)) throw new Error('scoreboard driver expects one certified cell')
33	  const scoreboard = await scorekeeper.leaderboard({ group: 'scoreboard-e2e' })
34	  const facts = await scorekeeper.facts(certified.report.sessionId)
35	  const exported = await scorekeeper.exportFacts({ sink: jsonlFileSink('./facts.jsonl') })
36	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify({ type: 'result', leaderboard: report.leaderboard, scoreboard, facts, exported })}\n`)
37	} finally {
38	  await ctx.fiber.dispose()
39	}

1	/**
2	 * Package-owned invariant: a facts record states what its own log says. Three
3	 * relations are recomputed from the durable events on every stamp, goal, or
4	 * verification change — `runsRecorded` equals the number of `verification/run`
5	 * events, `certified` agrees with the reward the trajectory fold decided, and
6	 * a certificate's isolation equals the isolation its `environment/run` stamp
7	 * declared, so a scoreboard row keyed by the stamp can never blend a
8	 * certificate earned under a different isolation level.
9	 *
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper/invariant
11	 */
12	
13	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
14	import type { InvariantFailure, InvariantInstaller } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants'
15	import type { Session, SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	import { foldVerification } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification'
17	import { foldSessionFactsState } from './fold.ts'
18	import type { SessionFacts } from './types.ts'
19	
20	const PACKAGE_NAME = '@deepseek-ai/dsh-scorekeeper'
21	
22	/** Cordis companion plugin name. */
23	export const name = 'scorekeeper-invariant'
24	/** Service required before the companion can reserve package ownership. */
25	export const inject = ['invariants']
26	
27	/** Event types that can change one of the checked relations. */
28	const DECIDING_EVENT_TYPES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
29	  'environment/run',
30	  'goal/change',
31	  'verification/standard',
32	  'verification/relaxation',
33	  'verification/run',
34	  'verification/certificate',
35	  'verification/directive',
36	])
37	
38	/**
39	 * Recompute every checked relation of one facts record against its log.
40	 * @param facts - the facts folded from `events`.
41	 * @param events - the durable events the record covers, in sequence order.
42	 * @returns one message per broken relation; empty when the record agrees with the log.
43	 */
44	export function factsDisagreements(facts: SessionFacts, events: readonly SessionEvent[]): string[] {
45	  const messages: string[] = []
46	  const outcome = facts.outcome
47	  const runs = events.filter(event => event.type === 'verification/run').length
48	  if (outcome.runsRecorded !== runs) {
49	    messages.push(`records runsRecorded ${outcome.runsRecorded} while the log holds ${runs} verification/run events`)
50	  }
51	  if (outcome.certified !== (outcome.reward === 1)) {
52	    messages.push(`records certified ${String(outcome.certified)} while the reward fold decided ${String(outcome.reward)}`)
53	  }
54	  const certificate = foldVerification(events).certificate
55	  const stamp = facts.identity.environment
56	  if (stamp !== undefined && certificate !== undefined && certificate.isolation !== stamp.isolation) {
57	    messages.push(`certifies at isolation "${certificate.isolation}" while its environment/run stamp declared "${stamp.isolation}"`)
58	  }
59	  return messages
60	}
61	
62	/** Validate one candidate event against the durable prefix that precedes it. */
63	function validateEvent(prior: readonly SessionEvent[], event: SessionEvent, fail: InvariantFailure): void {
64	  if (!DECIDING_EVENT_TYPES.has(event.type)) return
65	  const events = [...prior, event]
66	  let facts: SessionFacts
67	  try {
68	    facts = foldSessionFactsState(events).facts
69	  } catch (_malformedOutcomeStream) {
70	    // The goal and verification companions own their own malformed streams;
71	    // reporting the same event here would attribute it to this package too.
72	    return
73	  }
74	  for (const message of factsDisagreements(facts, events)) fail(`session event ${event.seq} ${message}`)
75	}
76	
77	/** Check existing sessions and every candidate event before Session publishes it. */
78	const install: InvariantInstaller = Object.assign((ctx: Context, fail: InvariantFailure) => {
79	  for (const session of ctx.sessions.list()) {
80	    const prior: SessionEvent[] = []
81	    for (const event of session.events) {
82	      validateEvent(prior, event, fail)
83	      prior.push(event)
84	    }
85	  }
86	  /* jscpd:ignore-start -- package companions share dispatch and registration plumbing */
87	  ctx.on('internal/dispatch', (_mode, eventName, args) => {
88	    if (eventName !== 'session/event') return
89	    const [session, event] = args as [Session, SessionEvent]
90	    validateEvent(session.events, event, fail)
91	  }, { global: true })
92	}, { inject: ['sessions'] })
93	
94	/**
95	 * Register the session-facts invariant companion.
96	 * @param ctx - Cordis context carrying the invariant service.
97	 * @returns the installed registration's disposer after setup succeeds.
98	 */
99	export const apply = (ctx: Context): Promise<() => void> =>
100	  Promise.resolve(ctx.invariants.register(PACKAGE_NAME, install))
101	/* jscpd:ignore-end */
